clue.text: After palaver, bets a rogue is to avoid dismissal

indicators.note: After puts the shuffled letters behind the word for palaver

parts.note: a palaver is a fuss or carry-on

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means behaving wildly, so the letters break ranks and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone, after a lot of fuss, places bets on a rogue in order to escape being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry-on is a British word for a fuss. To carry one's bat is cricket: an opening batter is still not out when the innings ends.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the phrase describes an opener surviving the whole innings, never getting out.

clue.text: Think party needs Republican to oust Liberal

indicators.note: to oust means one letter pushes the other out and takes its place

parts.note: to celebrate is to party

explanation.surface: A political party needs a Republican to drive out the Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cerebrate is a formal word for using the brain, considering things.

clue.text: Get hold of guards for a ticking off

indicators.note: guards means the first word stands around the second, protecting it

parts.note: to reach something is to get hold of it
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: An order to grab sentries who deserve a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproach is a rebuke, a telling-off for doing wrong.

clue.text: I agree to eat one thousand crumbs

indicators.note: to eat means the first word takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: yes is how one says I agree
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to eat a thousand crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumbs is not bread here but the mild British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of alarm or surprise.

clue.text: After half a month, character hasn't finished light work

indicators.note: After puts the cut-short character behind the half month

parts.note: the first half of November, four of its eight letters

indicators.note: hasn't finished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a letter is a character of writing

explanation.surface: Two weeks into the month, a writer has not finished a light piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Half a month is a half of a month's name, NOVE from November, not two weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short, usually lightweight or romantic novel.

clue.text: Reason for one to collar lousy youngster?

indicators.note: to collar is to seize round the neck, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: say is used like for one, introducing an example
a nit is the egg or young of a louse

explanation.surface: A teacher's reason for grabbing a scruffy, lice-ridden child.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind; losing one's reason is losing one's sanity.

clue.text: Mostly boring attending houses with lots of sex and violence?

definitions.text: with lots of sex and violence?

indicators.note: houses means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: at means present at, attending

indicators.note: Mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: dull means boring

explanation.surface: Going to lots of houses is mostly dull, unless they offer sex and violence.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult film or book is one rated for mature audiences because of explicit content.

clue.text: Strips this off outside in monokini

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
outside means just the two end letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone in a one-piece bikini strips this off.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmi, plural of isthmus, are narrow strips of land joining two larger areas.

clue.text: Maybe like a favourite child, not even taking precedence

indicators.note: taking precedence means the odd part comes first, before the child

parts.note: an odd number is one that is not even
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A parent's favourite child, who is never level-headed, gets priority.
explanation.walkthrough: Favourite here is the horse that bookmakers expect to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes a horse priced so short that it is expected to win, as the favourite usually is.

clue.text: Reversing roles, one may keep a watch on you

definitions.text: one may keep a watch on you

indicators.note: Reversing means the word for roles is read backwards

parts.note: parts in a play are roles

explanation.surface: Someone who swaps roles to keep watch on you, like a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch strap holds a wristwatch on the wearer's arm.

clue.text: Ex-PM has kedgeree on vacation, with foreign wine and fish

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a rudd is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A former prime minister eats kedgeree on holiday, with wine and fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Kevin Rudd was twice Prime Minister of Australia. Kedgeree is a rice, fish and egg dish.
explanation.definitionFit: He led Australia's government twice, so he is a former prime minister.

clue.text: What socialite does, having Sprite with the rich

parts.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a mischievous sprite
nobs are wealthy, upper-class people

explanation.surface: A socialite drinks Sprite while mixing with the wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprite looks like the soft drink, but it is a goblin.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, especially with important people, which is a socialite's occupation.

clue.text: Bit of rhetoric from student, one wholly using modern language?

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
I is the Roman numeral one
totes is current slang for totally

explanation.surface: A student uses trendy slang for a rhetorical flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech of understatement, as in 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Off home, a clergyman with a stutter?

parts.note: in means at home
a curate is a clergyman; a stutter repeats his first letter

explanation.surface: Away from home, a clergyman with a speech impediment.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure or estimate that is off is wrong, not correct.

clue.text: Tries to enter European club for performance

indicators.note: to enter means the first word goes inside the club's name

parts.note: Real Madrid is a European football club, often just Real
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: A rugby side scores tries to get into a European club for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tries is the court sense, as a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real show.

clue.text: Problem when walking in either side of canyon

indicators.note: in places the conjunction inside the canyon's two edges
either side of means the end letters at each edge of the word

parts.note: or pairs with either, as in either one or the other

explanation.surface: Hikers have problems walking along both rims of a canyon.
explanation.walkthrough: Either does double work: it pairs with OR, and with side of it picks both ends of canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot that makes walking hurt.

clue.text: Official beginning to make little bloomers in Arab land

indicators.note: in places the following letters inside the country

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word

parts.note: buds are flowers yet to bloom

explanation.surface: A functionary starts making tiny knickers in an Arab country.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers look like underwear but are flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate complaints against organisations.

clue.text: Polyglot losing stone eating cool Anglo-Italian food

indicators.note: eating means the shortened word swallows the next one
losing means the abbreviation for stone is taken out

parts.note: a linguist speaks many languages
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A language expert, having lost weight, eats a cool Anglo-Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglo-Italian because English often writes the -i ending where Italian has linguine.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is the anglicised spelling of linguine, a flat ribbon pasta.

clue.text: Going over section of awesome Times article

indicators.note: Going over says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reviewing part of an impressive newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece in a newspaper, a news article.

clue.text: Iranian heartlessly left, say, imprisoned

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letters are cut out, leaving the ends

parts.note: left is one example of a side

explanation.surface: An Iranian left the country cruelly, perhaps to avoid jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside is informal for in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inside is serving time in jail.

clue.text: Refuse to go here? Trick cyclist does number on bike half-cut

indicators.note: on means the number comes after the half bike

parts.note: a wheelie is a stunt riding on the back wheel

indicators.note: half-cut means the word is cut in half and only its front half kept

explanation.surface: A refusal at a stunt show, where a drunk cyclist performs a number on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse is the noun, rubbish, not the verb. A trick cyclist is also British slang for a psychiatrist. A wheelie bin is a British dustbin on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelie bin is a large household rubbish container on wheels.

clue.text: Day minus pants outside, practising this?

definitions.text: Day minus pants outside, practising this?

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters go around the day's letter
pants as a verb, rubbish, means awful, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Spending a day without underwear outdoors: is this naturism?
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British for underpants and also slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole day outdoors without underwear is what someone practising naturism would do.

clue.text: Scoundrel ordered goods

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, ordered
G is the abbreviation for good, so two goods are GG

explanation.surface: A scoundrel ordered goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an informal term for a rotten, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Czech maestro in team's playing around Albion's wingers

indicators.note: around means the shuffled team goes about the wingers
playing means the letters perform in a new order

parts.note: the outer letters of Albion, its two wings

explanation.surface: A conductor plays with a football team around West Brom's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion here is a football club like West Bromwich Albion; its wingers are its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was a Czech composer, of Ma Vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Constable used this when blocking slippery customer

indicators.note: blocking means the short word is lodged inside the other

parts.note: an eel is a slippery creature and an evasive person
as means when, as in as he left

explanation.surface: A police constable using something to block a slippery crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is not police but John Constable, the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand a painter uses to hold the canvas.

clue.text: Land owned bordering Germany's capital

parts.note: to land a fish is to bag it

indicators.note: bordering means the first word lies on both sides of the second

parts.note: had means owned
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Territory once owned on Germany's frontier near Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: Germany's capital looks like Berlin or G, but the 's is a link and capital the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.

clue.text: State formerly of America, with problem to the north

indicators.note: in a down answer, heading north means reading the letters upward

parts.note: Am is the abbreviation for America or American
a rub is a problem, as in there's the rub

explanation.surface: A former US state with a problem in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of Myanmar, a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Charles's bride-to-be exchanging cents for small vending machine

indicators.note: exchanging means one letter is swapped out for another
for gives what the cents letter is swapped with

parts.note: Lady Diana Spencer, Di Spencer, was engaged to Prince Charles

explanation.surface: Prince Charles's fiancée swapping coins for small change at a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser delivers items on demand, as a vending machine does.

clue.text: Picaroon's admitting a rubbish bard wrote these

indicators.note: admitting means letting the following letter in

parts.note: Picaroon is the setter, so Picaroon's is I'm
BS is a slang abbreviation for nonsense

explanation.surface: The setter confesses a hack poet wrote these lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare, the Bard, wrote largely in iambic pentameter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambs are metrical feet of a short then long syllable, the basis of Shakespeare's verse.

clue.text: Guy manipulated into sheltering criminal in hiding

indicators.note: sheltering means the outer letters hold the criminal inside

parts.note: a fella is a guy, a man

indicators.note: manipulated means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a lag is a convict, an old lag

explanation.surface: A man forced to protect a criminal who is lying low.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiding is a beating, not concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a thrashing, and flagellation is whipping as punishment.
